source_facts.fact: The current guideline was updated 16 June 2026 and says water companies in England and Wales must prepare and maintain a WRMP at least every five years and review it annually.
source_facts.gate: A WRMP is strategic supply planning and does not prove that a specific parcel can connect or has spare local network capacity.

source_facts.fact: The framework was last updated 15 April 2026 and sets long-term national and regional water-resources planning expectations.
source_facts.gate: National and regional planning evidence cannot be converted directly into parcel-level availability.

source_facts.fact: Official modelling states that without action public water supply deficit could reach up to 5,000 Ml/d by 2055, while non-public-water-supply sectors could add about 1,200 Ml/d demand by the 2050s.
source_facts.gate: Scenario totals are national planning values and must not be downscaled into parcel deficits or connection refusals.

source_facts.fact: The Secretary of State accepted the Environment Agency's 2021 determination of serious water stress areas.
source_facts.gate: The 2021 classification was produced for a specific regulatory purpose and is not a parcel-level 2026 supply-capacity measure.

source_facts.fact: Water undertakers wholly or mainly in England must prepare, publish and maintain statutory drought plans; the current guideline was published 16 June 2025.
source_facts.gate: Drought-plan actions and triggers are contingency planning, not proof of current restrictions at a site.

source_facts.fact: Sewerage undertakers have a statutory duty to prepare, publish and maintain drainage and wastewater management plans; the guidance uses company, river/local-authority and sewerage-catchment reporting levels.
source_facts.gate: DWMP risk and investment evidence is strategic/catchment evidence, not a parcel sewer-capacity decision.

source_facts.fact: Current guidance says draft DWMPs should be published by 1 November 2027 and final DWMPs by 31 August 2028, with annual review after publication.
source_facts.gate: Future publication milestones are not evidence that a proposed scheme is funded or delivered.

source_facts.fact: Environment Agency planning guidance for flood risk assessments and national standing advice was updated 28 May 2026.
source_facts.gate: Flood-zone or standing-advice screening alone is not a complete parcel planning decision.

source_facts.fact: The Environment Agency uses different percentile-based river-flow and rainfall/sea-level allowances for flood risk assessment depending on development type, lifetime and location.
source_facts.gate: Climate allowances are scenario inputs and must not be represented as measured future flood depths.

source_facts.fact: Ofwat's PR24 final determinations set the regulatory price, investment and service package for 2025 to 2030; company appeals/redeterminations must be versioned.
source_facts.gate: Company-level expenditure or performance commitments are not parcel-level water or sewer capacity guarantees.

core_rules: WRMP inclusion is strategic planning evidence, not a parcel water-connection offer
regional water resources plan evidence is not a site-specific capacity guarantee
national public-water-supply deficit scenarios must not be downscaled to a parcel
water-stress classification is not a site-specific refusal of water supply
drought-plan triggers are not proof that a drought restriction is currently active
planned drought restrictions are scenarios, not scheduled customer restrictions
supply-demand balance headroom is not identical to spare network connection capacity
resource-development option selection is not proof that a scheme is funded
funded water-resource infrastructure is not proof that it is constructed or operational
operational bulk resource capacity is not proof of local distribution-network capacity
PR24 expenditure allowance is not proof of delivery of a named local scheme
Ofwat price-control determination is not planning permission or environmental consent
DWMP risk band is not an individual-property sewer flooding prediction
DWMP company or catchment risk is not a parcel sewer-capacity result
DWMP investment need is not a committed construction programme
sewerage catchment boundary is not a cadastral parcel boundary
storm-overflow risk does not determine whether a parcel can connect to the sewer network
SuDS strategy requirement is not planning approval
requirement for a flood risk assessment is not an automatic planning refusal
Flood Zone classification is screening evidence, not an exact flood depth or velocity
Flood Zone intersection alone is not a complete planning decision
climate-change allowance is a planning scenario, not an observed future flood level
50th, 70th and 95th percentile allowances must remain distinct
central, higher-central and upper-end allowances must be chosen for the applicable development context
current flood mapping must not be treated as future-climate mapping without the prescribed allowance
modelled flood output must not be presented as a measured historic event
fluvial-model, tidal-model, fluvial-event, tidal-event and coastal-event evidence must remain distinct
source-protection-zone presence is not an automatic prohibition on development
groundwater protection risk is not proof that contamination exists on a parcel
abstraction licence availability is not a water-supply contract
regional water-resources group strategy is not a company WRMP
company WRMP is not the same document as a drought plan
drought plan is not the same document as an emergency drought plan
NAV duties do not prove that a specific NAV can serve a parcel
bulk-supply agreement evidence does not prove site-level distribution availability
compulsory metering policy context is not a measure of parcel water availability
water-stress classification and current drought status must remain distinct
river-and-sea flood risk must remain distinct from surface-water, groundwater and sewer flood risk
Environment Agency and lead-local-flood-authority responsibilities must remain distinct
national standing advice is not a site-specific Environment Agency consultation response
Environment Agency preliminary opinion is not formal planning approval
paid pre-application advice is not statutory consent
company-level PR24 performance commitment is not a local asset-condition measurement
sector investment totals must not be converted into parcel infrastructure capacity
CMA redetermination or appeal status must be versioned before using company allowances
2025-2030 regulatory-period evidence must not be applied outside its period without revalidation
source publication and last-updated dates must be preserved where status can change
final current guidance should outrank an earlier consultation where the consultation has been superseded
consultation evidence must not be represented as enacted or final policy
multiple pages from the same official publication are one evidence family, not independent corroboration
2021 serious-water-stress determination must not be relabelled as a new 2026 determination
dataset collector date is not automatically the effective date of every underlying entity
absence of public data is NO_DATA, not proof of no flood risk, no water stress or spare capacity
national statistics must not be downscaled to parcel facts without an explicit spatial relation
regional statistics must not be downscaled to site capacity without an explicit asset or supply-zone relation
exact parcel inference requires current authoritative geometry and an explicit intersection or service relation
research-only evidence must not create a Future Growth score while RECOVERY_PARKED
research-only evidence must not promote a parcel candidate while the predecessor gate is unresolved
a second or parallel shared runner must not be created for this continuation
no water, sewer, flood, planning or infrastructure capacity value may be fabricated
source-confidence score is research-source confidence and not parcel-level accuracy
